summary: Iter-28 verified Import-Progress stage tracking + 48h Lead Follow-ups. Backend pytest: 12/12 pass (test_iter28_followups_and_import_progress.py) in ~68s. Fast tests (~22s): default followups OFF + toggle persistence; cron auth 401 on no-auth and wrong-bearer, 200 <5s on correct bearer with X-Webhook-Id idempotency (duplicate:true on repeat); manual follow-up-draft on an email lead returns kind='no_reply' with real AI body (no placeholders), on a lead with prior replies returns kind='replied', and on a chat lead with empty from_email returns 400 with a friendly 'no email address' message; approve appends a reply whose 'by' contains '(follow-up)', delivery is email_sent/email_queued, followup.status becomes 'sent', and a second approve returns 404 'No follow-up draft to send'; dismiss sets followup.status='dismissed' and persists. Cron E2E (~21s): created a lead via /api/public/contact/{token} (after enabling preview), also seeded an archived lead + a no-email chat lead, back-dated all three to 72h in Mongo, enabled followups on a throwaway tenant, fired /api/cron/lead-followups with the WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET, and confirmed within ~20s the eligible lead got followup.status='draft' while archived and no-email leads were untouched; pending_drafts increased; a repeat cron with the same X-Webhook-Id returned duplicate:true; a fresh cron run did NOT re-draft the already-drafted lead; disabling followups_enabled and firing again left a fresh eligible lead untouched. Import Progress (~44s): /site/import-preview job walked scanning -> rebuilding -> done with stage_at timestamps and stage_detail populated on a live example.com scrape; result.source.pages >= 1. One-shot /site/import with mode='replace' produced result.applied.pages (business outcome verified) but the 'applying' stage was NEVER captured by 0.15s polling — a race between fire-and-forget say('rebuilding') in build_import and the awaited say('applying') in _run_job clobbers the applying write before any client can poll it (stage_at ~= finished_at, ~3ms apart in DB). Frontend Playwright smoke: login -> Vote Banner Test Co (app_bdbf27abe643) -> Inbox tab: followups-toggle flips ON, survives a full reload (needs to re-click tab-inbox-btn since tab state resets — matches iter27 note), and can be flipped back OFF. Only 1 inbox row exists (a chat lead) so followup-generate-btn / followup-draft-card / approve / dismiss UI wiring was NOT exercised end-to-end but data-testids and logic are covered by backend + code review. Site Mode -> web-import-btn opens the WebImportDialog, entering https://example.com and clicking Scan renders web-import-progress with all four import-step-scanning / -reading / -rebuilding / -applying rows visible, an active spinner on 'Scanning site', stage_detail '-> Starting import' and a '3s elapsed' counter — screenshot at /app/test_reports/pytest/iter28_stepper.png. Console had 2 x 404 warnings unrelated to iter-28 (asset misses on Inbox route, present in iter-27 too).

minor.issue: 'applying' stage window is effectively unobservable: build_import fires say('rebuilding') via asyncio.create_task (not awaited) and _run_job then awaits say('applying') immediately; the deferred 'rebuilding' task can execute after 'applying' commits, overwriting it. Even 0.15s client polling missed the window on a 1-page site. Business outcome (result.applied.pages) still correct, but the UI 'Applying pages' step will rarely animate. Fix: in _run_job._run_job.on(), await the task or gather pending stage writes before awaiting say('applying'). Alternatively: change on() to `await say(...)` (no create_task) or drain pending tasks via `await asyncio.sleep(0)` then explicitly overwrite stage after apply_import completes.

integration_issues.issue: After reload the Inbox tab is not re-selected (Overview loads by default) so the followups-toggle is not rendered until the user clicks tab-inbox-btn again. Persistence itself works. Consider persisting last-selected tab per-tenant in localStorage (raised in iter-27 too).

action_items: Fix 'applying' stage race: in web_import.py _run_job, ensure the fire-and-forget say('rebuilding') task cannot overwrite the awaited say('applying') update. Simplest patch: define `on` as `async def on(...)` and `await on(...)` throughout build_import/scrape_site (they are already awaited from an async context), OR keep the fire-and-forget pattern but wrap _run_job's applying update with `await asyncio.sleep(0)` after build_import and then `db.import_jobs.update_one({'job_id': job_id}, {'$set': {'stage':'applying','stage_detail':...,'stage_at': _now()}})` performed AFTER apply_import completes (before setting done) — so the write is not racing with delayed rebuilding.
Optional: persist last-selected AppDetail tab in localStorage so a reload keeps the user on the Inbox / Site Mode tab (also observed in iter-27).
critical_code_review_comments: web_import.py _run_job.on(): asyncio.create_task fires-and-forgets each stage write with no ordering guarantee vs subsequent awaited writes. Root cause of unobservable 'applying' stage. This same race can in principle cause 'reading' to overwrite 'rebuilding' on very slow LLM calls with fast scrape (unlikely but possible).

followups.py scan_due(): iterates apps sequentially and awaits each make_followup (each is an LLM call ~1-3s). With N eligible leads and M tenants, cron_runs.finished_at could lag many minutes — currently no limit per tenant (only global limit=40). Consider per-tenant limit and/or `asyncio.gather` with a small concurrency ceiling to keep total cron work under a few minutes.

followups.py cron_lead_followups: cron_runs dedupe is by run_id only. If a partner scheduler retries the same job with a NEW UUID, work is redone. Not a bug per spec ('run_id idempotency'), but tenants may see a duplicate draft attempt on a re-fired lead if the previous run crashed mid-way — mitigated by the `followup: {'$exists': False}` filter in scan_due (verified: a fresh cron did NOT re-draft an already-drafted lead).

followups.py _draft() 'replied' branch: the prior context only pulls the last 2 replies (fine) but truncates each at 800 chars; long back-and-forth threads may lose earlier user objections. Non-blocking.

followups.py followup_approve: mutates msg['followup'] in-place via {**msg['followup'], 'status':'sent'}; the drafted_at is preserved, but sent_at is added, so history is retained — good. But if body is edited on approve, the ORIGINAL drafted body is lost (only the edited text is stored). Consider keeping draft_body separate for audit.
InboxPanel.jsx: followups-pending badge only renders when > 0 — a user can't confirm 'no drafts pending' at a glance. Minor UX.

WebImport.jsx ImportProgress: relies on stage strings matching IMPORT_STAGES exactly ('scanning','reading','rebuilding','applying'). If backend emits an unknown stage (e.g. 'queued'), findIndex returns -1 and Math.max(0,-1)=0 highlights 'scanning' — visible early flicker on queued->scanning transition. Cosmetic.
web_import.apply_import mode='replace' still calls db.pages.delete_many with no undo path — same finding as iter-27.

rca of the issue: Applying-stage race: In web_import.py, `_run_job` builds an `on(stage, detail)` callable that schedules `say(stage, detail)` as a fire-and-forget asyncio task. `build_import`/`scrape_site` call `on('scanning'|'reading'|'rebuilding', ...)` via this pattern. When `build_import` returns, one or more of those DB update tasks may still be pending in the event loop. `_run_job` then does `await say('applying', ...)` (direct await, not via `on`) and immediately `await apply_import(...)`. Because apply_import for a small site is very fast (<50ms), and any pending 'rebuilding' write can complete between the applying write and the final 'done' write, the DB state observed by any poller is either 'rebuilding' briefly, then 'done'. Confirmed empirically: even 0.15s poll intervals fail to see 'applying'; DB stage_at == finished_at within ~3ms. Mitigation: convert `on` to an awaited coroutine (all callers of `on()` in scrape_site/build_import are already inside async functions) OR after `await build_import(...)` do `await asyncio.gather(*pending_stage_tasks)` before awaiting the applying write.
